items.title: Vanishing of Hom into a complex supported below the projective amplitude, and the resulting unique splitting
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The statement draws three consequences from a projective amplitude hypothesis on one object of the derived category: maps from it into a complex whose cohomology vanishes high enough are zero, every distinguished triangle with it as the third term splits, and in the strongest case the splitting is unique (statement lines 19703-19718). The proof chooses representatives adapted to both hypotheses, so that the two complexes have disjoint supports, reads off the vanishing of the Hom group through the identification of maps from a bounded complex of projectives, and then applies the splitting criterion of triangulated categories, with uniqueness coming from the same vanishing applied to a morphism of the split triangle (proof lines 19720-19740). The choice of representatives is what reduces all three assertions to one computation. The counted span refers four times, twice to results of this chapter and twice to results of other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.
